D:\\Users\\Eric Liu\\Documents\\Paradox.before: Harvests, fishing boats and grain merchants sustain life in the towns. A rise in food prices can carry a dispute from government offices into the streets. Food must reach the markets at prices townspeople can afford.

D:\\Users\\Eric Liu\\Documents\\Paradox.before: Canning allows food and fish to be stored longer, bringing purchasing, processing and long-distance transport into a single trade. Merchants can wait for better prices, while workers hope the factories will offer employment beyond the harvest season.

Our overlord has given its assent to domestic reform. The government may pursue changes to public appointments, military administration and representation while the subject relationship remains in force.

[SCOPE.sCountry('jp_partner').GetNameNoFormatting] has provided development funds. The grant will support construction and the training of skilled workers. Further funding of this kind will be unavailable for three years.

Our overlord has authorized negotiations for union with the other Japanese subjects. Our envoys may now approach them, though each invited government must still consent to the union.

The government has chosen expansion to the west, but the proposed tributary arrangement with Ili has not taken effect. Commanders and merchants can still pursue a western policy, drawing on the troops, revenues and support presently available.
